chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'May Allah have mercy upon a servant who makes us beloved to the people and does not make us hateful to them. By Allah, if they were to narrate the beauties of our speech, they would be more honored by it, and no one would be able to attach any fault to us. But one of them hears a single word and degrades it tenfold.'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for narrating hadith to ensure the Imams are loved by people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the critical role of the narrator (rawi) as a bridge between the Imam and the public, warning that a single poorly transmitted word can negate ten good ones. This principle underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *dabt* (precision) and *balagha* (eloquence) in hadith transmission, ensuring that the Ahl al-Bayt remain beloved (*mahbub*) rather than objects of ridicule or misunderstanding among the masses.

en.hubeali: H 14741 – Humeyd bin Ziyad, from Al-Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Wuheyb Bin Hafs, from Abu Baseer who said:

I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘May Allahazwj have Mercy upon a servant who makes usasws to be loveable to the people, and does not make usasws to be hateful towards them. But, by Allahazwj, they are reporting ourasws beautiful words to be honoured by it, and there is no leeway for anyone that he should attach anything to these (our wordsasws), but one of them hears the words, so he degrades the beauty of these words by ten times (by dropping ourasws words from himself)’.
en.sarwar: 293. Humeyd bin Ziyad, from Al-Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Wuheyb Bin Hafs, from Abu Baseer who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying: ‘May Allah (azwj) have Mercy upon a servant who makes us (a.s.) to be loveable to the people, and does not make us (a.s.) to be hateful towards them. But, by Allah (azwj), they are reporting our (a.s.) beautiful words to be honoured by it, and there is no leeway for anyone that he should attach anything to these (our words (a.s.)), but one of them hears the words, so he degrades the beauty of these words by ten times (by dropping our (a.s.) words from himself)’.
